ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account is overwhelmingly rank-constrained in non-brand: Search impression share is single digits (5–7%) while impression share lost to rank is 93–95% across the three in-scope non-brand campaigns, with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization. Auction position data corroborates this: competitors show top-of-page far more often (competitor 73.2% vs self 15.2%) and are above you most of the time (avg position-above-rate 85.4%). A secondary efficiency issue exists inside non-brand/long-tail where spend is concentrated on low-intent or low-quality terms (e.g., “insurance company phone number” QS 3.0, €2,605.80 spend, €1,371.47 cost/conv) while several high-QS commercial terms still have ~94–95% lost to rank.
notable_patterns: Non-brand demand is not being captured due to rank, not budget: Auto/Home/Life have 0% impression share lost to budget but 93–95% lost to rank, with budget utilization only 56.2–58.5% and impression share only 5–7%.
You’re materially losing the competitive auction: avg top-of-page rate self is 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%, and avg outranking share is only 9.1% while competitors are above you 85.4% of the time.

Several high-quality, high-intent keywords still show extremely low impression share due to rank (e.g., “auto insurance germany” QS 9.0 with only 5.0% IS and 95% lost to rank; “home insurance cost” QS 8.5 with 5.5% IS and 94.5% lost to rank). This points to insufficient bid/ad-rank in competitive auctions rather than a relevance problem on those specific terms.

Spend leakage/inefficiency is present on low-quality informational/service queries with very poor cost per conversion (e.g., “insurance company phone number” QS 3.0, €2,605.80 spend, €1,371.47 cost/conv; “what is life insurance” QS 4.5, €858.99 spend, €613.56 cost/conv), which likely depresses portfolio efficiency while still not fixing the rank deficit on core commercial queries.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 6% impression share with 94% lost to rank and 0% lost to budget, while budget utilization is 57.2%—you’re not entering/clearing enough auctions at competitive ad rank. This aligns with auction data where competitors’ top-of-page rate (e.g., Bluewave 76.7%) dwarfs your 12.1–18.4% range.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase ad rank on the highest-intent auto terms (prioritize the QS 8–9 terms already relevant) via bid floors and tighter query focus; simultaneously cut waste from low-intent/service queries to fund higher bids where it matters.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 5% impression share with 95% lost to rank and the lowest average QS among the non-brand set (4.1), indicating both competitiveness and relevance/landing-page alignment issues are holding top placements back. Budget isn’t limiting (0% lost to budget; 58.5% utilization).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Restructure home intent (quote/cost/comparison) into tighter groups with dedicated ad/landing alignment to lift QS, then raise bids selectively on the highest-intent segments once QS improves.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 7% impression share with 93% lost to rank and extremely weak average QS (2.0), suggesting the campaign is fundamentally not meeting relevance/experience thresholds needed to compete—raising bids alone may be expensive until QS is fixed. Budget isn’t the issue (0% lost to budget; 56.2% utilization).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Pause or sharply restrict low-intent life queries and rebuild around core commercial “comparison/quote” intent with new creatives and landing-page alignment to recover QS before scaling bids.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix non-brand ad rank where demand exists: raise bids on the high-intent, high-QS terms that are still losing ~94–95% to rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across the three non-brand search campaigns, impression share is only 5–7% while impression share lost to rank is 93–95% (and 0% lost to budget, with only 56–59% budget utilization). Even your strongest commercial keywords are barely serving due to rank: “auto insurance germany” (QS 9.0) has 5.0% IS with 95% lost to rank; “home insurance cost” (QS 8.5) has 5.5% IS with 94.5% lost to rank; “car insurance quote” (QS 8.0) has 6.0% IS with 94% lost to rank; “life insurance comparison” (QS 7.5) has 7.0% IS with 93% lost to rank. Auction data is consistent with a competitiveness gap: your top-of-page rate is 15.2% vs competitors at 73.2% and competitors are above you 85.4% of the time.
recommended_steps: Set bid floors / aggressive bid adjustments specifically on the four high-intent keywords above (and their close variants) until top-of-page presence materially increases.
Concentrate bids on exact/phrase for quote/cost/comparison intent first; reduce broad matching on research/service intent until rank improves on the revenue-driving core.
Use impression-share lost to rank and top-of-page rate as the guardrails: keep increasing bids only where these improve without collapsing ROAS.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate on non-brand moving from ~15% toward 25%+ while non-brand search impression share rises from 5–7% toward 12%+ (with lost-to-budget still ~0%).

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for low-intent/service queries dragging non-brand efficiency; reallocate to commercial ‘quote/cost/comparison’ demand
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: A meaningful slice of spend is tied up in very poor-converting, low-quality queries: “insurance company phone number” (QS 3.0) spent €2,605.80 at €1,371.47 per conversion; “home insurance claims process” (QS 4.0) spent €2,248.95 at €244.45 per conversion; “what is life insurance” (QS 4.5) spent €858.99 at €613.56 per conversion. Meanwhile, core commercial terms with strong QS (8.0–9.0) are still losing ~94–95% of impressions to rank, so wasted spend is directly competing with your ability to fund the bids needed to win those auctions.
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives for support/service/informational themes (e.g., phone number, claims process, what is, definition, customer service) in non-brand campaigns; keep brand/service handled separately if needed.
Tighten match types so ‘quote/cost/comparison’ terms don’t share budgets with informational queries; isolate high-intent ad groups/campaigns.
Move the freed spend into the high-intent segments where you are rank-limited (the QS 8–9 quote/cost/comparison terms).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost per conversion on non-brand trending down materially (target: cut the worst offenders like ‘phone number’ traffic by 70%+ of spend) while conversions on quote/cost/comparison segments rise.

recommendation_cards.title: Rebuild Life Insurance relevance first (QS 2.0 average): fix landing/ad alignment before scaling bids
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Search - Life Insurance has an average quality score of 2.0 and still loses 93% of impression share to rank (with only 7% IS). You also have demonstrably inefficient life informational traffic (“what is life insurance” QS 4.5, €858.99 spend, €613.56 cost/conv), suggesting intent mismatch that will keep QS and ad rank suppressed.
recommended_steps: Split life insurance into tightly themed segments (e.g., comparison/quote vs informational) and restrict bidding to commercial intent until QS recovers.
Write dedicated ads and send to a life-specific quote/comparison landing experience to improve expected engagement and relevance signals.
Pause/negative informational life queries that consume spend without sales intent (e.g., ‘what is …’, ‘definition’, ‘explained’).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Life campaign average QS moving from 2.0 toward 4.0+ and impression share lost to rank decreasing from 93% toward <85% (with stable or improving cost/conv).

recommendation_cards.title: Reduce competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage that’s inflating impressions without engagement
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: 48.3% of search-term impressions are coming from competitor-brand zero-click terms, totaling 35,700 impressions (e.g., “bluewave insurance”, “harborline mutual”, “crestfield direct”), while only one competitor term is shown converting (“nordkreuz insurance quote”, 1 conversion). This is a large share of exposure that is unlikely to help you recover non-brand rank where you’re already losing 93–95% to rank.
recommended_steps: Add competitor-brand names as negatives across non-brand campaigns (keep an exception list only if you intentionally run conquesting).
If conquesting is desired, isolate it into its own campaign with capped bids/budget and tailored ad copy, so it doesn’t dilute core non-brand efficiency.
Monitor search terms weekly to catch new competitor variants and misspellings.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms falling from 48.3% toward <15%, while CTR and conversion rate for non-brand improve.

already_working: Budget is not currently the limiter: every campaign shows 0% impression share lost to budget, and budget utilization is only ~51–58% (e.g., Non-Brand Auto 57.2%, Home 58.5%, Life 56.2%, Brand 52.2%).

Ad creation quality is generally solid: 80% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good out of 5), so the biggest lever is auction competitiveness and query mix rather than a wholesale ad rewrite.

Brand coverage is relatively strong compared to non-brand: Brand Search - DE has 85% impression share with only 15% lost to rank and strong ROAS of 4.7, so the urgent opportunity is non-brand scale/efficiency rather than brand protection.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Non-brand is currently being outcompeted on Ad Rank at exactly the moment when Germany insurance search demand and spend are accelerating. Category-level benchmarks show materially higher impression share than the account is achieving, while competitor intelligence indicates large rivals are investing heavily (and across channels) in search-led acquisition—raising the near-term risk that the account’s already-single-digit non-brand impression share remains suppressed or worsens unless bids/QS/query focus are fixed immediately.

supporting_facts.fact: Insurance in Germany: Spend Growth QoQ = 18.0%, Query Demand Growth QoQ = 12.0%, and Vertical-Avg Impression Share = 21.0% (Vertical | Highlighted Market table, p.5).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: With category spend and demand rising now, staying rank-constrained (93–95% lost to rank) means missing a growing pool of high-intent auctions; acting now to lift Ad Rank captures incremental demand while it’s expanding.

supporting_facts.fact: Germany (pilot account market): Search Spend Growth QoQ = 18.0% and Vertical-Avg Impression Share = 21.0% (Market | Search Spend Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share table, p.7).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A 21% vertical-average impression share vs the account’s 5–7% in non-brand signals a large immediate gap that is likely driven by rank competitiveness; the market is getting more expensive/competitive as spend grows, increasing urgency to correct bids/QS/query mix now.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword trend: “home insurance cost” index rises from 100 (Q4 2025) to 119 (Q3 2026), Growth = 19% (Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth table, p.6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This directly matches one of the account’s high-intent terms cited as losing ~94.5% to rank; demand is growing for that exact query theme, so improving rank on ‘cost/quote/comparison’ terms now has compounding payoff.

supporting_facts.fact: Bluewave Insurance: Spend Share = 24%, Active Creatives = 48, Channels = Search, Social, Display (Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels table, p.6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports the auction-pressure narrative behind high lost-to-rank: major competitors are scaling investment and creative volume across channels, raising the bar for Ad Rank (bids + relevance). Delaying makes it harder/costlier to regain top-of-page presence.

supporting_facts.fact: Crestfield Direct: Spend Share = 15%, Active Creatives = 29, Channels = Search, Social (Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels table, p.6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Reinforces that multiple competitors—not just one—are materially funding search acquisition, consistent with the account’s poor auction position metrics; urgency is higher when competitive intensity is broad-based.

supporting_facts.fact: Search accounts for 38% of category spend (Channel | Share of Category Spend table, p.7).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Because search is the single largest measured category channel share, under-serving due to rank constraints has outsized impact on growth; reallocating away from low-intent queries to fund higher Ad Rank on core commercial non-brand is urgent.
